input.brief: Estudio colombiano que hace apps con IA que te enseñan y no te reemplazan; producto principal MyWorld, un entorno para escritores donde la IA nunca escribe por ti

direction.name: The name as a monument
direction.idea: The name is the headline. Set it so large that it becomes architecture: as wide as the viewport, cropped by an edge, or stacked to fill the screen. Nothing else on the first screen competes; the description of what this is drops to a single small sentence. The idea comes from treating the name's letters as material. Ask what the subject can do to its own name: a photograph of the work sits inside a counter or replaces a letter, the name repeats down the page like a reel, the letters are split to opposite corners and the page happens between them. In the study this was the single most common device among sites scoring 7.5 or more.
direction.composition: First screen: the wordmark spans 88–100% of the viewport width (font-size 16–24vw, set with a clamp so it never wraps), anchored either to the bottom edge with its descenders nearly touching it, or dead centre with everything else pushed to the corners. One line of supporting text at 16–20px sits in a corner on a shared margin; navigation is three or four words in the opposite corner. After the hero the page is deliberately small and calm: a narrow text column or a simple two-column grid, so the contrast with the monument holds. The name returns once more at full width as the footer, in the inverse colours. Margins are tight (20–32px) so the type reaches the edges. Two type sizes do nearly all the work: the monument and a small text size, with one mid size for section headings.
direction.typography: One family. The display cut must survive enormous sizes: tight tracking (-0.04 to -0.07em), leading 0.8–0.9, optical kerning on. Section headings are modest (28–40px) on purpose.
direction.colour: Two values carry the page (ground and ink). The accent, if used at all, appears on one thing only: the single action or the inset image frame. The footer inverts ground and ink.
direction.imagery: Few images, used as inserts in the typography rather than as illustrations beside it: one photograph inside or behind the name (a 4:5 or 1:1 frame replacing a letter, or tucked between two words), then a short run of large full-width or half-width photographs further down. Square corners. No collage of small thumbnails.
direction.richness: Scale. The size of the name against the smallness of everything else is the entire visual event, so protect both ends: do not shrink the name to make room, and do not let body text creep above 20px.
direction.pitfalls: A long name set small is just a logo. If the name has more than about 12 characters, stack it on two lines or crop it with the viewport edge; never drop below 12vw. Do not add a second big headline under the name. Do not decorate the letters.

hero.name: Name across the middle
hero.blueprint: Paper and ink only; no picture on the first screen. The name runs on one line across the vertical centre, sized to span from the 18px left margin to the 18px right margin (97.5% of the width). Set it as inline SVG text with a `viewBox` fitted to the word and `width: 100%`, or tune its vw size to the letter count, so it never wraps. In a heavy grotesk the letters stand about 280px tall, from about 310px to 590px; nothing touches or overlaps them. The four corners carry everything else on 18px margins. Top-left: one supporting sentence at 18px on two lines, max 36ch, and 16px below it the single action as a solid ink rectangle. Top-right: a menu word or three text links at 15px. Bottom-left, on a baseline 24px above the edge: the city or the kind of work at 16px. Bottom-right on the same baseline: two or three text links at 15px. The ground between the corners and the name, about 230px above and below it, stays empty and is closed on both sides by the corner texts. The name returns in the footer at the same width with ground and ink swapped and a two-line invitation above it, so the page closes like a bracket.
hero.mobile: The name stays on one line across the width inside 16px margins and moves up to 22% of the height. The supporting sentence follows on the left margin at 17px, then the action at full width. The lower half holds the first picture of the work as a 4:5 frame cropped by the bottom edge, so the screen does not end in empty paper. A menu word sits top-right.
hero.headline: The name itself on one line, up to about 12 characters; the 18px sentence in the top-left corner says what it is.

type.note: A tall, condensed high-contrast serif whose capitals read like a masthead or a shop fascia. Suits residences, hotels, restaurants and wine, where a short name can stand floor to ceiling.

palette.name: Sand and moss
palette.note: Sand grey holds the page with charcoal type, and one deep leaf-green band may close it. Moss green is reserved for buttons; brighter greens and blues arrive only through photographs.

motion.name: Scaling wordmark
motion.description: The giant name responds to the scroll: as the first screen leaves, the wordmark scales down a few percent (or grows from 0.94 to 1 as the footer arrives) on a scroll-linked timeline, so the monument feels heavy. Travel stays under 8%. Static fallback where scroll timelines are unsupported. Recipe: 'Scroll-linked progress' in references/motion.md, animating `scale`.

sections.name: Title, note, facts row
sections.blueprint: First row: a heading of two to four words in a light weight at clamp(44px, 5vw, 76px) sits on the left margin in columns 1–6; a three-line paragraph at 16px, 260px wide, sits in columns 10–12 with its last line on the heading's baseline. Columns 7–9 stay empty. 120px lower, a second row sets three or four facts (a date, a time, a place, a price) as large light text at clamp(28px, 3vw, 44px), spread across the 12 columns with `justify-content: space-between`. Each fact has a one-line explanation at 14px directly under it in the soft ink, left-aligned to the fact. Facts are separated only by the space between them, so the row reads like the line of times on a printed programme. A photograph may start under the right half of the facts row, 5 columns wide at 4:3. Padding 140px top, 120px bottom.
sections.mobile: Heading at 11vw on the left margin; the note follows directly under it at 16px, full width. The facts become a two-column grid with a 32px row gap, each fact at 26px with its explanation beneath. Any photograph goes last, full width.

sections.name: Giant title, uneven wall
sections.blueprint: A one- or two-word title in capitals at clamp(72px, 9vw, 136px), leading 0.9, sits flush left at the 16px margin; on its baseline at the far right, one underlined link at 15px to the full archive. 32px below, thumbnails pack into an uneven wall with 8px gaps: a flex-wrap layout in which each row has a different fixed height (cycle 240, 360, 200, 300px) and each tile's width follows its image ratio, so widths range from one-sixth to one-half of the page and tile edges do not line up between rows. Rows are justified to both margins with `flex-grow`. Under each image, one caption line at 12px: project name left, year in the soft ink right. Square corners; no hover overlay beyond a slight dimming of the other tiles. Holds 9–16 projects. The section ground is one flat colour, dark or saturated, edge to edge.
sections.mobile: Title at 17vw on one line. The wall becomes rows of alternating composition: one full-width tile, then two tiles splitting the width 62/38, then 38/62, with 6px gaps and fixed row heights of 220 and 150px. Captions stay as one line under each tile.

sections.name: Run-in column
sections.blueprint: The quietest sequence: one reading column and good typography. A single column 520–600px wide starts at about 30% of the viewport width (or sits on the page's text axis). The heading is a two-to-five-word question or statement at 28–32px, 48px above the first paragraph. Three to five paragraphs follow at 17–18px with line-height 1.6. Each opens with a bold run-in phrase in full ink that names its moment ('To begin,', 'Within a day,', 'After that,', 'From then on,') while the rest of the paragraph runs in the soft ink; there are no subheads, bullets or markers. After each paragraph, 20px lower, comes one small piece of evidence exactly as wide as the column: a cropped interface fragment, a photograph at 16:9, or a row of three small frames 96px tall. 72px separates stages. Nothing in the section is wider than the column, and the space to its left stays empty.
sections.mobile: The column fills the width between 20px margins. Type stays at 17px. Evidence pieces keep the column width; the row of three frames becomes a single sideways-scrolling row 88px tall. 56px between stages. The heading drops to 24px.

sections.name: Pinned title, portraits pass
sections.blueprint: A wrapper tall enough for its portraits: about 90svh per person, up to six people. A `position: sticky; top: 0` layer of 100svh holds the heading, two words at clamp(88px, 12vw, 180px), leading 0.85, centred at mid-height, in white with `mix-blend-mode: difference` so it reads over ground and photographs alike. Beneath it in the stacking order, portraits scroll past in normal flow: each a 4:5 photograph 26–30vw wide, alternately starting at column 2 and ending at column 11, 60svh apart, so each one passes behind a different half of the heading. Under each portrait's left corner: the name at 18px, the role at 14px in the soft ink, and one sentence of up to 30 words in a 280px measure. The last portrait is followed by 40svh of empty ground before the heading releases. Square corners. Nothing else is on screen.
sections.mobile: The heading shrinks to 17vw and pins 16px from the top instead of at mid-height. Portraits become 72% wide, alternating between the left and right margins, 48px apart, each with name, role and sentence beneath at the portrait's width.

sections.name: Address in display rows
sections.blueprint: The contact block is a stack of five full-width rows, every one set at the same size, clamp(44px, 6vw, 88px), regular weight, left-aligned with a 20px inset and leading 1.0: the building or venue name, the street, the city with postcode, the opening hours as one compact line, the phone number. Each row is about 150px tall with the text sitting in its lower third; rows are told apart by alternating two flat tones of the section colour as full-width bands, or by 28px of space alone. A sixth row holds a one-word greeting at the same size followed, 24px to its right and centred on the x-height, by a solid round button 0.9em across with an arrow, which opens the email or booking link. Street and phone rows are links (map, call). No heading and no form. Optionally, one small round photograph sits at the right end of the first row.
sections.mobile: Rows at 9.6vw with 16px insets, about 84px tall; the hours break onto two rows (days, then times). The greeting row becomes a full-width band in the accent colour with the round arrow button at its right end, 56px across.

references.name: NOTHIN’
references.idea: The studio's name set as a wordmark so large it is the whole hero, repeated in inverted colours as the footer, so 'nothing' is literally the only content on screen.
references.hero: The captured hero frame is a black preloader wipe; this describes the loaded state. White field. A custom heavy geometric wordmark in black spans the full width between 1% margins, vertically centred, about 30% of the viewport tall, its apostrophe hanging at the top-right. Top-left: a two-line statement at about 1.6vw with a small black pill button under it. Top-right: a tiny menu label with a four-dot icon. Along the bottom edge: a one-line studio descriptor at left, two social links and a language chip at right. Everything else is empty white, with no image and no colour.
references.type: PP Neue Montreal medium for statements at up to about 5vw, sentence case, tight tracking and leading; the Book cut for small text; IBM Plex Mono for tiny grey project labels. The wordmark is custom heavy geometric lettering at close to 100vw. Only three text sizes: statement, caption, micro-label.
references.colour: #ffffff #000000 #2b47e6 #2f5d33 #bfbfbf — Strict black and white that flips by section: white hero and intro, black works and footer. The only colour comes from inside the imagery, chiefly electric-blue foil and fern green.
references.imagery: 3D renders of inflated chrome, crumpled blue foil and bubble-wrap hearts on black; project shots are brand mock-ups photographed in settings (a card among ferns, a laptop on a dark desk). Hard-edged rectangles of varied size, square corners.
references.layout: Margins of about 1%, so content runs nearly edge to edge. The intro is a left headline over a full-width black media panel; the works section places images at irregular widths and horizontal offsets with wide black gaps, each with a mono label and one-line caption above.

sections.description: White section. A two-line statement at about 5vw sits flush left under a small logo mark, filling the top quarter. Below it a black rectangle spans the full content width and runs off the bottom of the viewport, holding a 3D still life clustered at centre. On further scroll the panel shrinks to a small thumbnail docked top-right, while a parenthesised label and a four-line paragraph at caption size appear in two narrow columns at the left.

Black section headed by one bold uppercase word top-left. Project images are placed as a loose scatter: one at about 48% width hugging the left margin, the next narrow and hugging the right margin lower down, the next inset to start 18% across. Above each image sits a tiny grey mono project name, then a one-line white caption at about 1.1vw. A two-line aphorism floats alone at the right between projects. Long stretches of empty black separate items.

Black, full viewport. A two-line invitation at about 5vw at the left in the upper third, with two outlined pill buttons under it; three social links stacked at about 78% across. The wordmark repeats in white at full width, anchored to the bottom, with a single row of micro-text credits beneath it.

steal: Make the hero nothing but the name: a wordmark scaled to the full viewport width on a blank field, with only a two-line statement and one small button in a corner.
Repeat the hero wordmark in inverted colours as the footer so the page opens and closes on the same shape.
Place case-study images at different widths and horizontal offsets on a black field, each with a micro mono label and a single-line caption above it instead of a card.
references.media: No picture on the desktop first screen: a full-width black wordmark on white covers about 30% of the height. Then an inset showreel with 18px gutters scrubs down into a box in the right third as text arrives on the left, a staggered two-column mosaic of 48, 32 and 65% widths, a pinned full-bleed brand film with a blurred copy behind it as a halo, cut-out 3D objects on black with letters tumbling between them, and the wordmark again, inverted, as the footer; 17 images and 4 muted looping videos.
references.motion: The preloader (on the phone capture) morphs a 3D inflatable through three forms while a counter runs down to 000, then white rises in a hard-edged mask to reveal the wordmark. Lenis: the showreel scrubs at 3, works cards drift at their own speeds (y scrub 1.5, yPercent scrub 3), the film pins for one screen, heading letters split and scatter, and services letters and objects tumble in on power2.in at random 0.25-0.69s durations; the house ease is cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) at 0.5-0.6s.

references.name: House of Honey
references.idea: A block-heavy wordmark pierced by a hairline script: the bold-against-delicate contrast is repeated at every scale, with giant pink script behind quiet serif statements.
references.hero: Top 42% is a flat blush-pink band; the bottom 58% is a full-bleed photograph of a bright living room, arched window on the centre axis, butting against the band with no margin. A tiny nav row sits at the very top with 8px side margins: block logo glyph and five links left, contact link with a small square arrow box far right. The wordmark fills the width edge to edge: two words in ultra-black extended caps, about 120px cap height, dark aubergine, with a hairline script 'of' 230px tall between them, overshooting above and below. Directly beneath, two two-line serif uppercase taglines at 31px, one flush left, one flush right.
references.type: Wordmark in ultra-black extended caps; statements in noeText serif, uppercase, 31–40px, tight tracking; nav and captions in neueHaasGrotesk around 14px; 'canora' hairline script for the connecting word and for cropped background words at 37vw. Three contrasting voices, each with one job.
references.colour: #edccbe #331917 #0e0e0e #f26fcb #ffffff — Blush pink and dark aubergine-brown alternate as full fields and as each other's text colour. Hot pink appears only in the oversized script and a 2px divider. Photographs bring saturated colour.
references.imagery: Editorial interior photography, saturated and daylight-lit. Hero is a full-bleed landscape crop; projects are portrait crops about 5:6 in a three-column grid with 4px gutters and square corners.
references.layout: Edge-to-edge with 8px outer margins. Typographic sections (small centred label, serif statement, cropped giant script) alternate with a three-column image grid. Blush and brown fields swap each section; hairline link rows close blocks. The footer is a full-width logo glyph.

sections.description: Dark aubergine field under the hero photo, separated by a 2px hot-pink line. A small sans label centred, then a three-line centred serif uppercase statement at about 31px in blush, 45% of the width. Behind it a hot-pink script phrase set near 37vw runs off both sides and is cut by the section's bottom edge, its ascenders rising into the statement. A smaller serif line follows.

Title card before the project grid. Blush field, nearly empty screen. A small label and a one-line serif uppercase heading about 40px sit centred at 55% height. The giant pink script returns, cropped by the bottom edge so only its top half shows and running off both sides.

Three columns edge to edge with 4px gutters and 8px outer margins. Portrait photos about 500×580px, square corners. Under each: an uppercase sans title at 14px and a grey line of GPS coordinates. Two rows, then a full-width hairline row with a text link left and a small square arrow box at the far right.

Brown field. The logo glyph is enlarged to full width and about a third of the screen: blush rectangles and quarter-circle arcs with 4px gaps, forming an abstract monogram. Below: four columns of small links, a hairline, two addresses in the first two columns, another hairline, then copyright left and a small blush button right.

steal: Set a wordmark edge to edge in ultra-heavy extended caps and thread a hairline script connecting word through it that overshoots the cap height both ways.
Use an oversized script word in one hot accent colour as a cropped background layer behind small, calm serif statements.
Split a tagline into two halves, flush left and flush right on the same baseline under the wordmark, instead of centring it.
references.media: The lower 58% of the fold is a full-bleed interior photograph that continues for one full viewport as a five-image crossfading slideshow with a pink progress line on its bottom edge. Below: a three-up grid of 4:5 project tiles with 8px gutters sliding over a giant script marquee, a full-bleed tinted feature photograph with its title docked bottom-left, a full-bleed photograph with an inset colour card, and one giant cropped letterform as the footer's picture, the photographs oversized to 110-170% of their frames for drift and no video anywhere.
references.motion: There is no visible preloader and the page is whole at 400ms; under Lenis, blocks rise 8px and fade in over 800ms ease-out at 0-260ms staggers (39 WAAPI calls), slideshow crossfades take 600ms cubic-bezier(0.7,0,0.25,1), the oversized photographs drift, and script marquees run on CSS time (90-122s per pair). Page changes use a 1s view transition on the same curve; nothing pins, and there is one reduced-motion rule.

references.name: Studio K95
references.idea: The whole portfolio is one WebGL room: project images orbit in rings around a chrome voxel rose inside an electric-blue gridded cylinder.
references.hero: A saturated ultramarine field covers the viewport, drawn with a faint dark grid that curves as if seen from inside a cylinder. At centre floats a chrome, stair-stepped 3D rose about 57% of the viewport height. Around it some twenty project images sit as upright planes on three horizontal rings: stamp-sized along the top and bottom, two large portrait ones flanking the rose, each angled toward the centre. Interface text is tiny and pinned to the edges with 58px margins: logo top left, a pill layout toggle top centre, three caps links and a language switch top right; a discipline line, a works counter and the year along the bottom.
references.type: One wide-set grotesk ('adaptive' in the digest) at a single small size, roughly 14 to 16px, bold, caps for nav and labels. No display headline is shown; the digest's 32px heading is not visible. The blocky geometric logo is the only large letterform.
references.colour: #0800b7 #1500e1 #c8ccd4 #ffffff #e9e34a #e23a28 — One electric blue fills everything; white type and chrome geometry sit on it, and every other colour arrives through the project thumbnails. A single yellow dot marks the cursor.
references.imagery: Project stills (posters, packaging, furniture, brand marks) as square-cornered portrait planes in 3D perspective, uncropped and ungraded, plus a reflective chrome voxel rose as the centre object.
references.layout: A single non-scrolling screen. Content lives in 3D space while a thin heads-up frame holds three items across the top and three across the bottom, with nothing between them but the canvas. Scrolling rotates the scene rather than moving the page.

sections.description: The index is the scene itself. Scrolling or dragging spins the rings so different thumbnails swing to the front and scale up to roughly 40% of viewport height, while the rest recede to stamp size at the edges and corners. Hovering a plane attaches a small translucent pill to the cursor with an arrow, the project name and its discipline. A segmented pill at top centre switches the arrangement between rings and a spiral.

There is no footer block, only a single baseline 30px above the bottom edge carrying three items in the same small bold type: the studio's discipline flush left, a counter of shown versus total projects at centre with one underlined word linking to the full list, and the copyright year flush right. Thumbnails pass behind this line as the scene turns.

steal: Let a single saturated colour field be the whole page and take every other colour from the work thumbnails.
Offer two named arrangements of the same index through a small segmented toggle, so the layout itself becomes a control.
Keep interface text to one small size pinned at the corners and centre edges, including a live count of shown versus total projects.
references.media: WebGL covers the whole fold: about 25-30 portrait project cards (3:4, square corners, shown as photographed) on three rings round the camera, roughly 35-40% of the pixels, round a central chrome rose (about 15%), on a gridded ultramarine field. The focused card is pulled to the front at about 3x its neighbours' size, and a glass label beside the cursor names it; no DOM images and no video.
references.motion: Readable in about 1.2s with no preloader: the canvas fades in over 0.7s ease and the label switches from a scroll prompt to the focused project by 2.5s. The page never scrolls: the wheel, smoothed by Lenis, turns the card rings round the camera while the rose spins from face-on to edge-on about every two steps, as continuous inertial rotation with no reveals, and label lines enter over 0.95s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), with cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) and (.4,0,.2,1) as the house eases and 9 reduced-motion queries.
